title: Build Query String
prompt: A TypeScript client builds URLs from filter objects. Write a function that skips undefined values, sorts keys alphabetically, encodes keys and values, and returns a query string without the leading question mark.

explanation.beginner:
Example: buildQueryString({"page":2,"q":"react"}) produces "page=2&q=react". The result must follow this precise rule: A TypeScript client builds URLs from filter objects. Write a function that skips undefined values, sorts keys alphabetically, encodes keys and values, and returns a query string without the leading question mark. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “skips undefined values”: input [{"q":"js"}] produces "q=js". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
